requirement:
For a response with exactly one `submit_result` call, arguments other than an
object containing only the `result` field receive a tool error describing that
expected structure. The model can resubmit in the same conversation. Decoding
the field's value into `R` follows
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.judge.submission.decoding`.
rationale:
structural: The text of `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.invalid` states only observable behavior. (1) "arguments other than an object containing only the `result` field receive a tool error describing that expected structure." This is an input-to-output rule. A hand-written check, a schema validator, or a serde struct with `deny_unknown_fields` would all give the same tool error, so the text does not prescribe a library, type, signature or named interface. (2) "The model can resubmit in the same conversation." This is conversation-lifecycle behavior. Any harness that keeps the conversation open meets it, and the text names no structure that must hold it open. (3) "Decoding the field's value into `R` follows {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.judge.submission.decoding`." This is a citation that supplies context. The decoding rules, such as decoding directly as `R`, belong to that cited requirement and are judged against its own text, not this one. No clause fixes how the implementation is built, and there are no review roots. No structural obligation needs implementation evidence here.

behavioral: The obligations are: (1) arguments that are not an object containing only `result` get a tool error describing the expected structure; (2) the model can resubmit in the same conversation; (3) decoding the `result` value is governed by the cited `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.judge.submission.decoding`, so it needs no separate test here.

The tests cover these as follows:
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[malformed_submissions_receive_feedback_and_can_be_corrected]` drives the full agent loop with `{}`, `{"other":true}` and `{"result":{},"extra":true}`. Those are the missing-field, wrong-field and extra-field cases. For each one it asserts that the follow-up request carries a tool result with `is_error` set. It asserts that the feedback names "exactly one field named `result`". It then scripts a corrected second submission and asserts that it is accepted. The accepted answer is `Decision::No` and the vetting callback runs once, which shows the conversation stayed open for resubmission.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tools.rs#mod[submission_tests]/fn[submission_envelopes_require_one_result_field]` checks the envelope validator `submitted_value` directly. It covers non-object arguments (null, array, string, bool) and the empty, wrong-field and extra-field objects. It asserts the exact error message. It also asserts that valid `{"result": x}` envelopes pass the value through unchanged.

The non-object argument classes are tested only at the unit level, not through the agent loop. A search showed `submitted_value` is the function that validates the envelope. The loop test shows its error reaches the model as a tool error, so no separate loop-level test is needed. The decoding cases (missing field, wrong type, unknown variant, non-JSON string) are also exercised in the loop test, and they belong to the cited decoding requirement. I found no gap.

text: For a response with exactly one `submit_result` call, arguments other than an
object containing only the `result` field receive a tool error describing that
expected structure. The model can resubmit in the same conversation. Decoding
Decode the submitted `result` directly as `R` and invoke vetting callbacks only
for successfully decoded answers. If decoding fails, return the decoding error
and guidance on the expected `result` to the model as a tool error. Keep the
conversation open for a corrected submission.
